ingredients.item: fresh lotus root, peeled, cut into 1 cm coins
rice vinegar , in the soaking water
toasted sesame seeds ; 1 dried red chili or a pinch of gochugaru , optional

instructions.heading: Step 1
instructions.action: The coins and everything but the sesame finish into a wide pan — soy, water, syrup, mirin, garlic, chili — brought to a simmer, lid on, medium-low.
instructions.visualOrTactileCue: a gentle bubble, not a boil: the braise should barely tremble. A hard boil breaks the coins' shape before they tender.

instructions.heading: Braise 25–30 minutes, turning the coins once at the halfway mark
instructions.action: Braise 25–30 minutes, turning the coins once at the halfway mark, lid on until the last five minutes. The braise reduces slowly while the root drinks.
instructions.visualOrTactileCue: the doneness read: a paring knife or chopstick slides into a coin's flesh with gentle resistance — tender-firm, never soft, and the thinnest coins' edges have gone translucent amber. The braise by now has reduced to a syrup that pools in the pan's low spots.

instructions.heading: Lid off, the final reduction — 5 minutes
instructions.action: Lid off, the final reduction — 5 minutes, turning the coins through the thickening syrup every 60 seconds until every face wears glaze and the pan is nearly dry. Off the heat: sesame oil, seeds.
instructions.visualOrTactileCue: the coin test: bite through and the holes should visibly hold glaze; the flesh gives with a fine, almost crisp-firm grain (lotus keeps a faint snap even fully braised — its signature), savory-sweet through and through.

storageNotes: Keeps 4–5 days refrigerated and improves for two days as the coins keep drinking — the elegant make-ahead. Serve at room temperature or lightly warmed; the glaze is best not reheated hard.
Variations: the same braise on potato (#B09) and quail eggs (#B19); honey swapped in runs a deeper gold; a garnish of julienned red chili over the coins for the holiday table's full architecture.
